newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Communication gap stalls Sino-British diplomacy.
newsitem.headline: Communication gap stalls Sino-British diplomacy.

text.p: Chinese and British diplomats negotiating details of the handover of Hong Kong failed on Wednesday to achieve a meeting of minds -- or even a meeting.
Chinese negotiators waited in vain for over an hour for British diplomats to turn up for the talks.
As he gave up waiting, Chinese team representative Chen Zou'er told reporters: "We regard that the British changed their minds and decided not to come to the meeting."
The diplomats were members of the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group which is responsible for hammering out details of the transition of the British colony to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
A British spokesman said it was all a misunderstanding and the Chinese had been notified the day before that the talks had been rescheduled.

"What happened was that yesterday we rescheduled the talks which were to have been held this morning... perhaps there is some communication gap. Obviously, there is," British Foreign Office spokesman Bill Dickson said.
